# Ze

> Open, programmable network OS for Linux. Ze speaks BGP, IS-IS, and OSPF, manages interfaces, programs the FIB, and gives operators a CLI, web UI, telemetry, looking glass, API, and plugin system around one coherent configuration model.

Built for people who want a network stack they can inspect, automate, and extend. ExaBGP users get a migration path to a more performant codebase. Pre-release: no tagged versions yet, built continuously from the main branch. AGPLv3 open source.

Every link below points at that page's Markdown source (an `index.md` sibling of its `index.html`, plain content, no HTML to parse); the `(web: ...)` link is the same page rendered for a human, for when a link needs to be shown to one.

## Project

- [Features](https://ze-software.github.io/ze/features/index.md): 46 features, color-coded by category (web: https://ze-software.github.io/ze/features/)
- [CLI Reference](https://ze-software.github.io/ze/cli/index.md): 380 commands, generated from the live binary (web: https://ze-software.github.io/ze/cli/)
- [Configuration Reference](https://ze-software.github.io/ze/config-reference/index.md): The whole config as a searchable index: 35 sections from live YANG (web: https://ze-software.github.io/ze/config-reference/)
- [Dependencies](https://ze-software.github.io/ze/dependencies/index.md): 39 direct packages, generated from go.mod (web: https://ze-software.github.io/ze/dependencies/)
- [Performance](https://ze-software.github.io/ze/performance/index.md): Measured BGP benchmarks, not claims (web: https://ze-software.github.io/ze/performance/)
- [Compare](https://ze-software.github.io/ze/compare/index.md): How Ze stacks up against BIRD, FRR, and more (web: https://ze-software.github.io/ze/compare/)
